source.title: Investigating the Role of Overparameterization While Solving the Pendulum with DeepONets

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present, though the plotted curves are not legible in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests double-descent claims using DeepONets on the pendulum task, with sweeps over model size, training-set size, optimizer, and label noise; this is a different model and application setting from the original deep-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative outcomes for model-size and training-set-size sweeps and for label-noise conditions. The figures are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text, so rows record only the authors' explicit textual descriptions. The iteration-based losses are compared across model sizes; the paper does not report a test-error curve swept over epochs.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps model size in DeepONets (ReLU MLP branch and trunk nets) on a pendulum operator-learning task. It varies training-set size, optimizer and training-label noise, and reports whether test error peaks at the interpolation threshold, whether more data hurts, and whether triple descent appears. This is a new setting with direct results on V1, V3 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Additions: the abstract says best test error shows only very mild double descent. High training-label noise largely removes the stochastic-Adam best-loss double descent, at the cost of no benefit from overparameterization. The authors recommend reporting best loss over iterates rather than end-point loss for DeepONets.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses DeepONets with a pendulum differential-equation task, varying network size, training-set size, optimizer, and training-label noise; the original source studies standard deep-network settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern varies with best loss versus average endpoint loss, deterministic-Adam versus stochastic-Adam, training-set size, and training-label noise.
record.peer_reviewed: The Symbiosis of Deep Learning and Differential Equations (DLDE) NeurIPS 2021 Workshop
record.problems: The supplied text does not expose numerical values from the plotted curves or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use one application and one DeepONet architecture family; the authors note that asymmetric architectures and more complicated problems remain future work.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numeric curve values could be extracted because the figures are not legible in the supplied text. No other eligible outcomes were omitted.

untested.parts: No test-error-over-epochs curve is reported; only best-over-iterations and last-10^4-iteration averages are given.
Only DeepONets are studied; no non-deep model classes.
Optimally tuned regularization is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Workshop paper with qualitative, figure-based claims only. There are no numbers, no error bars and one architecture family (symmetric depth-4 nets with m=100). States rest on the authors' conclusion text. V4 links were removed because DeepONets are deep networks; V1 covers them.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not provide exact peak locations or numerical error values for each plotted model size.
No test-error curve over training epochs or iterations is reported; best loss over iterations and average loss over the final 10^4 iterations are compared across model sizes.
Only training sets of 1000 and 5000 samples are compared; the text does not give numerical effects or a detailed peak location.
Only DeepONets on the pendulum problem are studied, not a broad range of model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested as predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Label-noise effects and the possibility of triple descent are examined. Optimally tuned regularization is not tested.
The study does not re-express complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.

source_check.notes: The findings are qualitative: significance is not accompanied by statistical tests, and the high-noise cutoff is unspecified. Section 2.3 reports an available implementation and accompanying data despite the pack's code=n.

statements.correction: High training-label noise largely suppresses stochastic-Adam best-loss double descent; overparameterization then provides no lower-test-error advantage. statements.problem: The study's findings and noise levels are accurately reported, but the challenges framing assumes that V6 predicts stronger peaks with increasing noise. V6 does not state that monotonic prediction.
